traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Balsaminaceae: leaves alternate, opposite or whorled; leaves simple; margins entire, crenate or serrate; veins pinnate; blades linear, oblong or ovate; stipules usually absent, sometimes present; leaf rosettes basal or none; plants hermaphrodite; flowers turned over usually absent, often present; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems herbaceous; flowers solitary or in cymes; flowers zygomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule or drupe; parts of each whorl 5; stamens 5; carpels 5. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
